history.summary: The 'Hemavati Shiva Temple' row maps to the Hemavati group of ancient Shiva temples, whose principal shrine is the Sri Siddeshwara (Siddheswara) Swamy Temple - notable for depicting Shiva in seated human form in yoga posture rather than as a linga. Hemavati (Henjeru) was the capital of the Nolamba Pallavas, and the temple group (Siddeshwara, Doddeswara - an ASI Monument of National Importance, and Mallikarjuna) was built by Pallava and Nolamba kings between the 7th and 10th centuries, with a glorious phase under King Iriva Nolamba Diliparaja (940-969); the temple's 72-line inscription documents the clan, its Shaiva dharma and the education system it supported. CSV town corrected from Anantapur to Hemavati (village near Madakasira); district corrected from Anantapur to Sri Sathya Sai. Sources disagree on the distance from Anantapur city (40 km vs 140 km - unreliable; Hemavati is ~34 km from Madakasira per gktoday). Hours listings conflict slightly (5 AM-8 PM vs 5 AM-7 PM - verify). Coordinates (14.03 N, 77.00 E, wikimapia) are village-level, approximate.

name: Hemavati Shiva Temple
town_description: Hemavati (also Hemavathi/Henjeru) is a village near Madakasira in Sri Sathya Sai district, on the Andhra-Karnataka border along the Hiriyur-Madakasira route. It was the capital of the Nolamba Pallava dynasty and is known for its group of 7th-10th century Shiva temples, an ASI-protected site with an on-site archaeological museum.
